title: Cocharacter orbit extensions and limit subfunctors
statement: Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field], $G$ a $k$-group scheme [def-sc-group-scheme], and $\lambda:\mathbf G_m\to G$ a group-scheme homomorphism, with $\mathbf G_m$ and the affine line as in [def-sc-gm-ga]. For a commutative $k$-algebra $A$ and $g\in G(A)$, an orbit extension is an $A$-morphism $q:\mathbf A^1_A\to G_A$ whose restriction along $\mathbf G_{m,A}\hookrightarrow\mathbf A^1_A$ is $t\mapsto\lambda(t)g\lambda(t)^{-1}$; scalar extensions use the fibre product [def-pc-fibre-product]. Define $P_\lambda(A)$ as the subset of $G(A)$ of points admitting an orbit extension. Define $U_\lambda(A)$ as the subset admitting such an extension with $q(0)=1$. Define $Z_\lambda(A)$ as the subset of points $g$ such that, for every commutative $k$-algebra $B$, every $k$-algebra map $f:A\to B$, and every $s\in B^\times$, the image $g_B$ commutes with $\lambda(s)$. These are subfunctors of the functor of points of $G$ under the usual scalar-extension maps; no reducedness, finite-type, smoothness, connectedness, or algebraic-closedness hypothesis is imposed.

source.place: Definition 13.21 and Proposition 13.24, pp.261--262 (orbit extension); Proposition 13.29 and definitions of P(lambda), U(lambda), Z(lambda), pp.263--264.
